title: Claude Hopkins's band and Babe singing with him
summary: Thomas spent a year or more with Claude Hopkins at Roseland. Babe recalls working with him at the last Uptown Cotton Club show and the Howard, and Joe describes his slow comedy.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So do you go from him to Benny Carter?
No, with Claude Hopkins.
Oh, Claude Hopkins next. Where was Claude?
Claude was working at Roseland.
How long were you with him?
I'd say maybe it was a year, Baby?
I'd say it was about a year.
Tremendous musician.
I like him, too. A lot of people find Claude sort of dry but I like him. We'd laugh. Funny guy. But, don't you think he's sort of a funny personality.
Him? Are you kidding?
JT (1 of 2)
I got to laughing with him.
Talking about Claude Hopkins.
Yeah, we're talking about Claude Hopkins.
(well I tell you...)
Did you sing with Claude?

Not Only as a singer in the band but, you know, Stanley, at that time theaters were very much alive so I worked with Claude at different times in different theaters. I had a couple of incidents where I worked with Claude. I worked with Claude at the Howard Theater in Washington, D. C. and I also worked with Claude at the fx last show, it was the first time I ever worked with Claude, the last show that they did at the old Cotton Club. Oh, I'm dating myself terribly.
Uptown?

Uptown, the last show. I was always getting in on the end, the every end of everything, here I come because that era was fading away and I'm a kid coming up. But, I made the end of it. I worked with Claude on that and then I worked with Claude at the Howard Theater in Washington.
How long were you with Claude then?
Me? Let me give you an idea about Babe. Now you've got to get her expression. Babe was never a Band singer.

Babe was a personality on her own. She was a feature performer with Lunceford, the Harlem Express, a feature performer. ... Hop, I guess it might have been a year and one-half but he was a tremendous person, tremendous musician. Lot of comedy.
JT (1 of 2)
